 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT ADMINISTRATIVE

  B. ARTS AND HUMANITIES MONTH PROCLAMATION

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. You
  will receive a 30-second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to the clerk before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please
  state your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2019  2
   A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of September 17, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 654 AMENDING
  TITLE XI, SECTION 110 THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICPAL CODE- BUSINESS
  LICENSES

  Adoption of the referenced Ordinance No. 654 amending Title XI, Section 110
  of the San Gabriel Municipal Code will add a provision for exempting certain
  performers at City sponsored events and any Community Services recreation
  program individual instructors, coaches and/or referees from business license
  fees, add a provision for prorating business license fees for non-San Gabriel
  vendors at City sponsored events, and correct various business license fees to
  match the amount adopted with Ordinance No. 356-C.S. on July 16, 1991. No
  business license taxes are being added or increased.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading, read by title only,
  and adopt at the 2nd reading, Ordinance No. 654 amending Title XI, Section 110
  of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, pertaining to Business License Taxes.

  D. CALIFORNIA FOR ALL- COMMUNITY EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAM
  (CERT) AND LISTOS CAPACITY BUILDING GRANT

  The San Gabriel Fire Department has been awarded grant funds in the amount
  of $20,000 from the 2019 California For All Emergency Preparedness Campaign.
  This is designed to help Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) and
  LISTOS (Spanish for Ready) programs. The San Gabriel Fire Department will
  apply these funds towards engaging San Gabriel community members in

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2019  3
   emergency and disaster preparedness. The award of the grant will require a
  budget amendment for receipt and use of the grant funds.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-46, increasing
  the revenue estimates and appropriations (transfer out) in the Other Grants
  Fund (186) by $20,000 to receipt and transfer the funds and increasing the
  revenue estimate (transfer in) and appropriations by $20,000 in Capital/Special
  Project Funds (account number 124-761-57-96-341). Staff further recommends
  that the City Council authorize the Interim Fire Chief to accept the California
  For All CERT and LISTOS Capacity Building Grant and purchase the items within
  the confines of the City’s purchasing policy.

  E. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 653 – ZONE TEXT
  AMENDMENT TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING
  TO ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS (PLANNING CASE NO. ZTA19-001)

  At the September 17, 2019 City Council meeting, Ordinance No. 653 was
  introduced by a 5-0 vote. Adoption of this Ordinance would delete references
  to previous accessory unit options, provide clarification to Accessory Dwelling
  Units (ADU) development, and add a requirement for a covenant to be recorded
  with all future ADU applications.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive the reading in full; and
  2. Adopt Ordinance No. 653, an Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  San Gabriel Amending Chapter 153 (Zoning Code) of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code Relating to the Development of Accessory Dwelling Units
  (ADUS).

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 19-40 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE REQUEST FOR
  BLOCK PARTY - 371 N. DUANE AVENUE

  The Public Works Department received a request from Carla J. Seifi for a
  temporary street closure. The purpose of this event is to hold a block party on
  Saturday, October 19. 2019, from 4:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. in the 300 block of N.
  Duane Avenue. The closure will take place between Sycamore Drive and Adelyn
  Drive only. Resolution No. 19-40 details the location, date and times for the
  closure, as well the conditions that must be followed by the applicant. The

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2019  4
   Public Works, Fire, and Police Departments have reviewed and approved the
  request.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-40 authorizing
  closure of the 300 block of North Duane Avenue between Sycamore Drive and
  Adelyn Drive from 4:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. on Saturday, October 19, 2019.

  G. RESOLUTION NO. 19-44 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE AT 851 E.
  GRAND AVENUE BETWEEN GLADYS AND THE RUBIO WASH ON OCTOBER
  5, 2019

  The Public Works Department received a request from the San Gabriel Valley
  Humane Society for a temporary street closure for a 95th anniversary
  celebration on Saturday, October 5, 2019 from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. on Grand
  Avenue between Charlotte Avenue and the Rubio Wash. The closure will take
  place at 851 Grand Avenue between Charlotte Avenue and the Rubio Wash.
  Resolution No. 19-44 details the location, date and times for the closure, as well
  the conditions that must be followed by the applicant. The Public Works, Fire,
  and Police Departments have reviewed and approved the request.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution 19-44 authorizing
  closure of Grand Avenue between Charlotte Avenue and the Rubio Wash from
  7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. on Saturday, October 5, 2019.

  H. LS-1 OPTION E AGREEMENT WITH SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON (SCE)
  TO REPLACE HIGH PRESSURE SODIUM VAPOR STREET LIGHTS WITH
  LIGHT-EMITTING DIODE (LED) STREET LIGHTS CITYWIDE

  On June 1, 2015, the LS-1 Option E tariff became available to cities for street
  light (LED) retrofits. This program allows Southern California Edison (SCE) to
  replace High Pressure Sodium Vapor (HPSV) street lights with more efficient
  LED street lights with no out-of-pocket capital cost to cities. Instead, initial
  capital costs will be amortized through energy cost savings over a 20-year
  period. SCE owns and maintains 460 street lights throughout the City of San
  Gabriel (City) along residential and arterial streets. The City pays SCE a monthly
  facility fee for each pole which includes the cost of electricity and required
  maintenance. The annual City’s budget for the subject street lighting is
  approximately $66,493. These types of street lights are referred to as LS-1 lights
  and fall under SCE’s LS-1 cost tariff.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2019  5
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve an LS-1 Option E agreement with SCE to replace High Pressure
  Sodium Vapor (HPSV) street lights with Light Emitting Diode (LED) street
  lights; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute the Southern
  California Edison Company Schedule LS-1 Option E, Energy Efficiency-Light
  Emitting Diode Fixture Replacement Rate Agreement.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT (MOA) WITH SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS

  During the September 17, 2019 City Council meeting, staff presented a wildlife
  management update which included several alternatives for the City Council to
  consider, including a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the San Gabriel
  Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG). Should City Council approve the
  MOA, it will provide the City of San Gabriel with services related to the Regional
  Coyote Management Network (RCMF) for a cost of $20,000 for the next two
  years.

  Recommended Action:

  City Council to approve the Memorandum of Agreement and authorize $10,000
  to be transferred to from the General Fund contingency account to pay for the
  implementation of the agreement.

  B. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE HISTORIC PRESERVATION AND
  CULTURAL RESOURCE COMMISSION

  On August 15, 2017, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 636 to amend
  provisions of the San Gabriel Municipal Code (SGMC) Chapter 153 (Zoning
  Code) relating to historic preservation and cultural resources (Attachment A).
  Adoption of the Ordinance capped a multi-year effort to modernize and
  strengthen the SGMC in an effort to protect historic resources in the city,
  preserve San Gabriel’s heritage for future generations, promote public
  education, participation and appreciation of historic preservation and preserve

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 1, 2019  6
   diverse and significant architectural styles as well as historic preservation
  objectives. The Ordinance was praised and/or recognized by the San Gabriel
  Historical Association, Pasadena Heritage, American Planning Association – Los
  Angeles, Los Angeles Conservancy, and California Preservation Foundation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the role of the Commission and
  provide direction to staff on whether any changes need to be made. If this
  direction would result in the need to amend the existing Historic Preservation
  and Cultural Resource Ordinance, direction to initiate a ZTA is required.

  C. PRESENTATION ON THE PUBLIC WORKS CITYWIDE MAINTENANCE
  PROGRAM

  The City of San Gabriel (City) owns and maintains the majority of infrastructure
  within the public right-of-way. Public Works staff is responsible for
  constructing, maintaining and preserving City-owned infrastructure including
  streets, sidewalks, the sanitary sewer system, the stormwater system, traffic
  signals and signs, street lights, pavement markings, public landscape and trees,
  parks, and City facilities. Staff desires to present the City Council with an update
  on the new Public Works proactive citywide infrastructure maintenance
  program.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Update.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 11. ADJOURNMENT
